title: Gideon and the Veil
premise: Marguerite Ashgrove, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, keeps ledgers for a guild that trades in impossible things — debts of luck, borrowed years, stolen names. When prayers to the old gods begin being answered again, each answered prayer leaves a hollow where a memory used to be, and Marguerite discovers her own past is being spent to fuel them. The culprit is the Veil: an ancient hunger wearing King Aldric like a crown, feeding on the city's remembered griefs through the long winter. To save him and the city, Marguerite must break her own oath, rally the guild's debtors as unlikely allies, and unbind the king in a reckoning where justice is demanded outside any law. In the end she pays her final memory — her name — to close the Veil, and the guild gives her a new one, making her belonging something chosen rather than owed.
about_author: G. M. Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forgotten legal documents before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who keep accounts — of money, of memory, and of the heart.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Marguerite audits the guild's winter accounts, trading a bottled lullaby and a borrowed shadow while hiding her swordspeaker's oath beneath clerk's ink. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; she belongs to the ledger but not to anyone.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered on Copper Street
chapters.summary: A widow's prayer for rain is answered impossibly — but she no longer remembers her son's face. Marguerite investigates, finding frost blooming indoors in autumn. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: first dread; the impossible has a price, and someone is collecting.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes the Crown
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane summons Marguerite: the king has requested the guild's oldest contract, sealed before his grandfather's reign. She recognizes the seal — it matches the frost sigils. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: unease deepening into suspicion; the law and the guild are entangled.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Crown
chapters.summary: At the palace, Marguerite meets King Aldric, whose eyes flicker between warmth and winter. The court physician privately begs her help: the king forgets hours at a time. POV: alternating Marguerite and the physician. Emotional beat: pity curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Oathbound
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Marguerite swears the swordspeaker's oath, binding her blade to truth and forbidding her from striking the crowned. POV: Marguerite (past). Emotional beat: the cost of belonging to an order that no longer exists.

chapters.title: Debtors' Winter
chapters.summary: Marguerite quietly gathers the guild's debtors — a luck-thief, a woman who sold her grief, a boy made of borrowed years — trading favors for loyalty. POV: rotating among debtors. Emotional beat: found family forming in the margins of the law.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: A cathedral congregation prays and wakes with empty childhoods; the Veil feeds openly now. Marguerite traces the answered prayers to ley-lines converging beneath the palace. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: grief at scale; the city is being eaten politely.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane reveals he has been selling memories to the palace for decades to keep the guild alive — including pages of Marguerite's own past. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: betrayal; her belonging was purchased with pieces of herself.

chapters.title: Names Are Not Free
chapters.summary: The luck-thief teaches Marguerite how the Veil spends what it takes: every memory becomes a prayer answered, every answer strengthens the crown. POV: the luck-thief, then Marguerite. Emotional beat: understanding the enemy's mechanics; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The King in the Snow Garden
chapters.summary: Marguerite reaches Aldric alone; for one clear hour he begs her to kill him before winter finishes falling. Her oath forbids striking the crowned. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: compassion trapped by duty; the oath becomes a cage.

chapters.title: Breaking the Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite burns her own account pages to sever Corvane's claim on her memories, exiling herself from the guild's protection. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice; choosing justice over safety.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Snow buries the city mid-autumn; prayers go unanswered now because the Veil is sated and hunting larger prey — the king's whole self. POV: multiple citizens. Emotional beat: despair; time running out.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: The debtors convene a rogue tribunal in the guildhall to judge the Veil, since no court can try a god. Marguerite argues the case herself. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: purpose; the theme crystallizes — law fails, justice must not.

chapters.title: The Verdict of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: The tribunal rules the Veil may be unbound only by a willing payment greater than its hunger. The boy of borrowed years volunteers; Marguerite refuses to let him. POV: the boy, then Marguerite. Emotional beat: moral weight; protecting the found family.

chapters.title: Into the Undercroft
chapters.summary: Guided by the ley-lines, the company descends beneath the palace to the Veil's root — a throne of ice grown around the original oath-stone of the swordspeakers. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: awe and terror; her order's history is complicit.

chapters.title: What the Oath Hid
chapters.summary: The oath-stone shows the truth: the first swordspeakers bound the Veil with their own memories, and Marguerite's oath was designed to deliver her here as the next payment. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: fury and clarity; she was always meant to be spent.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Marguerite speaks her sword free of the oath, shattering the vow that forbade striking the crowned, while the debtors hold the ley-lines open against the Veil's counterattack. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: liberation through broken vows.

chapters.title: King and Hunger
chapters.summary: In the ice throne's heart, Marguerite fights the Veil wearing Aldric's body, refusing to kill the man inside it — instead naming every memory the Veil stole until it must answer for them. POV: Marguerite and Aldric. Emotional beat: the climax's turn; memory as weapon.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: To close the Veil, Marguerite pays her greatest remaining treasure: her own name and all memories attached to it. The Veil collapses; Aldric wakes, freed and weeping. POV: Marguerite, dissolving. Emotional beat: sacrifice fulfilled; identity surrendered.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: Winter breaks. Aldric, remembering everything, publicly pardons the guild and outlaws memory-debt; Corvane faces the new tribunal he never expected. POV: Aldric, then the debtors. Emotional beat: justice rendered outside the old law, gently.

chapters.title: A New Name, Freely Given
chapters.summary: The debtors gather and give the nameless Marguerite a new name, written in the ledger not as debt but as gift. She stays — not oath-bound, but chosen. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: belonging earned and offered; warmth after the long cold.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Epilogue: spring trade resumes; a child brings a prayer to the guildhall asking if gods still listen. Marguerite writes a careful answer in the ledger and smiles. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: quiet hope; some things are worth keeping accounts of.
